questions.q: What does the “rack and pinion” mechanism do in a private car?
options: Filter air for the engine
Convert the rotation of the steering wheel into movement that turns the wheels
Split power between the front and rear axle
Control the movement of the springs
questions.explain: A small gear (the pinion) turns a toothed bar (the rack), which moves the wheels on both sides through the tie rods.

questions.q: What does power steering do?
options: Make turning the steering wheel easier, using hydraulic pressure or an electric motor
Prevent wheel lock when braking
Connect the two sides of the suspension
Adjust the camber angle
questions.explain: Power steering adds assistance to turning the wheel, so even turning on the spot feels light and natural.

questions.q: The engine stops while you’re driving. What happens to the steering?
options: The steering locks completely and can’t be turned
The steering still works, but needs much more force than usual
There’s no change to the steering at all
The steering becomes lighter than usual
questions.explain: Without power steering (engine off or a faulty pump) the steering can still be turned, but needs much more effort.

questions.q: What is the camber angle?
options: The angle at which the front of the wheels points inward or outward, seen from above
The angle at which the wheel tilts inward or outward, seen from the front
The angle of the sway bar
The angle between the steering wheel and the front wheels
questions.explain: Camber is the tilt of the wheel inward or outward seen from the front; toe is the angle seen from above.

questions.q: What can change the wheel alignment, even without visible damage?
options: A hard hit in a pothole or riding up onto a kerb
Washing the car
Driving at a reasonable speed on a smooth road
An engine oil change
questions.explain: A pothole hit, riding onto a kerb, or a minor collision can change the alignment angles even without an outward sign.

questions.q: A tyre is more worn on its inner edge than its outer edge. What does this usually indicate?
options: A camber problem
Pressure too high
A worn shock absorber
A slipping clutch
questions.explain: Uneven wear between the inner and outer edge of a tyre usually indicates incorrect camber.

questions.q: The steering wheel points straight, but the car drifts slightly to one side even without touching the wheel. What is this?
options: A sign of a torque converter fault
Pulling to one side — a possible sign of inaccurate wheel alignment
This is normal behaviour in every car
A sign of a clutch problem
questions.explain: Pulling to one side while driving straight, even without touching the wheel, is a typical sign of incorrect wheel alignment or a suspension fault.

questions.q: What does the spring do in the suspension?
options: Carry the car’s weight and absorb shocks
Transfer force from the engine to the wheels
Connect the two sides of the suspension
Control the movement of the shock absorber
questions.explain: The spring carries the car’s weight and absorbs shocks from the road; the shock absorber is what controls its movement.

questions.q: What does the shock absorber do?
options: Connects the steering wheel to the steering mechanism
Controls the spring’s movement, so the car doesn’t keep bouncing after a bump
Prevents wheel lock when braking
Carries the car’s weight on its own
questions.explain: The shock absorber controls the springs’ movement and stops the car bouncing repeatedly after a bump.

questions.q: What does the sway bar do?
options: Adjust the toe angle
Lock the wheels when parked
Absorb shocks from the road instead of the spring
Reduce the car’s sideways body roll in a sharp bend
questions.explain: The sway bar connects the two sides of the suspension and reduces the car’s sideways roll in sharp bends.

questions.q: How do you perform a “bounce test” to check a suspected shock absorber?
options: Push down hard on that corner of the car and let go, and see how many times it keeps bouncing
Check the colour of the brake fluid
Measure the tyre pressure
Drive at 100 km/h and check for vibration in the steering wheel
questions.explain: A good shock absorber stops the motion after one bounce or less; a worn one keeps shuddering and bouncing several times.

questions.q: Why can a worn shock absorber lengthen stopping distance?
options: It increases tyre pressure
It weighs the car down
It only interferes with the ABS
The wheel loses contact with the road for moments, and without contact there’s no friction to help stop the car
questions.explain: When a worn shock absorber makes a wheel lose contact with the road for a moment, there’s no friction at that moment to help stop the car — stopping distance lengthens, especially on a rough road.

questions.q: What do the control arm, ball joint and bushing do in the suspension?
options: Increase brake pressure
Transfer force from the engine to the wheel
Connect the wheel to the chassis and let it move up and down
Absorb moisture from the air
questions.explain: The control arm, ball joint and bushing connect the wheel to the car’s chassis, and let the wheel move up and down while staying attached.

questions.q: You hear a knock (“clunk”) every time you go over a bump. What does this usually indicate?
options: A worn wheel bearing
A worn brake pad
A worn control arm, ball joint or bushing
Inaccurate wheel alignment
questions.explain: A knock that repeats over bumps usually indicates wear in the control arm, the ball joint or the bushing.

questions.q: You hear a hum that gets stronger with speed, and doesn’t change with braking or turning. What does this indicate?
options: A clutch problem
A worn wheel bearing
Pressure too high
A spring brake problem
questions.explain: A noise that changes with speed alone, not with braking or turning, almost always points to a worn wheel bearing.

questions.q: What does vibration in the steering wheel at a certain speed usually indicate?
options: Wheel imbalance, an out-of-round tyre, or a warped brake disc
A slipping clutch
Low pressure in the brake fluid reservoir
A stuck parking brake
questions.explain: Vibration in the steering wheel at a certain speed usually comes from wheel imbalance, a damaged tyre, or a warped disc.

questions.q: What is “steering play”?
options: Strong pulling to one side when braking
Difficulty turning the steering wheel standing still
Constant vibration in the steering wheel at every speed
Excessive free movement in the steering wheel before the wheels respond
questions.explain: Steering play is excessive free movement of the wheel before the road wheels start to respond, indicating wear in the steering mechanism.

questions.q: A car “wanders” in its lane and needs constant steering correction. What is unlikely to be the cause?
options: Low tyre pressure
A worn tie rod
The daytime running lights indicator being lit
Inaccurate wheel alignment
questions.explain: Lane wandering is related to wheel alignment, tyre pressure or a worn tie rod — not to the daytime running lights indicator, which has nothing to do with steering.

questions.q: You hear a clicking noise only in a sharp turn, not while driving straight. Which system does this usually relate to?
options: The parking brake
The suspension system
The brake servo
The driveshaft (the CV joint)
questions.explain: A click that only appears in a sharp turn usually belongs to the driveshaft — a worn CV joint — not to the suspension system.

questions.q: What characterises a steering box, still common in heavy vehicles?
options: It doesn’t need power steering at all
It’s completely identical to the rack-and-pinion mechanism
It exists only in electric cars
It uses a worm gear instead of a straight rack
questions.explain: A steering box is an older steering mechanism, especially common in heavy vehicles, that uses a worm gear to convert the rotation of the steering wheel.

questions.q: What is the toe angle?
options: The distance between the two axles
The angle between the spring and the shock absorber
The direction the front of the two wheels point, inward or outward, seen from above
The tilt of the wheel inward or outward from the front
questions.explain: Toe is the angle at which the front of the two wheels points slightly inward (toe-in) or outward (toe-out), seen from above.

questions.q: What is the difference between a coil spring and a leaf spring?
options: There’s no practical difference between the two
A coil spring is common in private cars; a leaf spring withstands heavy loads and is common in trucks and buses
A leaf spring is common in private cars, and a coil spring only in trucks
A leaf spring is used only in a strut
questions.explain: The coil spring is the common one in private cars; the leaf spring is more resistant to heavy loads and common on the rear axles of trucks and buses.
